# The Simplest Case of New Truth Is Mere Addition

The simplest case of new truth is of course the mere numerical addition of new kinds of facts, or of new single facts of old kinds, to our experience--an addition that involves no alteration in the old beliefs.[^1] Day follows day, and its contents are simply added.[^2] The new contents themselves are not true, they simply COME and ARE.[^3] Truth is what we say about them, and when we say that they have come, truth is satisfied by the plain additive formula.[^4] But often the day's contents oblige a rearrangement.[^5]
